channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Why China’s 4.3% growth is worrying its government
item.description: It's the slowest growth since 2022, when China was still in the grips of the pandemic, and below the government's already-lowered annual target of 4.5-5%; the country is facing multiple challenges of a real estate slowdown, sluggish consumption, and serious challenges in the job market Why China’s 4.3% growth is worrying its government.

item.title: Shipwrecks of Shackleton and Scott recreated in 3D digital form after deep sea expedition
item.description: Canadian scientists visit remains of polar exploration vessels in ‘golden era for shipwreck investigating’Moments after devouring the final glimmers of light, the seafloor offered nothing but darkness and silt. Then the bow appeared.

item.title: NASA astronaut Anil Menon, two others reach International Space Station
item.description: The Roscosmos spacecraft carrying Anil Menon and Russian cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina lifted off from Baikonur at 8:17 pm IST on Tuesday (July 14, 2026) just as the orbital laboratory flew over the cosmodrome NASA astronaut Anil Menon, two others reach International Space Station.

item.title: Nepal’s new government, old concerns: Governance, dissent, shrinking civic space
item.description: After completing 100 days in office, the Balendra Shah administration now finds itself confronting many of the same questions that dogged its predecessor before last year’s Gen Z protests, which ultimately swept Mr. Shah to power Nepal’s new government, old concerns: Governance, dissent, shrinking civic space.

item.title: India turns to AI to improve healthcare access
item.description: In the second part of a series on India's artificial intelligence push, CNA looks at how hospitals are using AI to detect eye diseases and analyse medical scans, while doctors stress the technology remains a tool, not a replacement. India turns to AI to improve healthcare access.

item.title: China’s savvy pivot in courting Muslim Indonesia
item.description: Beijing’s long courtship of Indonesia’s Muslim communities reached a new milestone this month, when the Majelis Ulama Indonesia (MUI), the nation’s top body of Islamic scholars, traveled to China. The five-day “Digital Silk Road” program brought MUI council members to Guangzhou and Shenzhen, with a focus on technology, halal industries, education and cultural exchange. item.title: US Senate Unveils Revised Russia Sanctions Bill As Lawmakers Push To Cement Graham's Legacy
item.description: A bipartisan group of US senators on July 14 introduced the Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026, unveiling a revised package of sanctions and tariffs aimed at squeezing Moscow's war finances while seeking to overcome concerns that had stalled earlier versions of the legislation. US Senate Unveils Revised Russia Sanctions Bill As Lawmakers Push To Cement Graham's Legacy.

item.title: After Double Amputation, Ukrainian Vet Says 'Thirst For Independence' Led The Way To Recovery
item.description: Ukrainian soldier Artem lost both his arms in combat near Pokrovske, a frontline village in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. Recovering from his injuries has meant relearning how to do daily activities -- from getting dressed to working at a computer. After Double Amputation, Ukrainian Vet Says 'Thirst For Independence' Led The Way To Recovery.

item.title: Why The US-Iran Conflict Keeps Shifting Between Fighting And Diplomacy
item.description: As the US and Iran exchange new strikes, military analyst Jonathan Schroden explains why wars often become more violent before peace, how the Strait of Hormuz has become the conflict's strategic centre, and why drones are reshaping naval warfare. Why The US-Iran Conflict Keeps Shifting Between Fighting And Diplomacy.

item.title: Death toll reaches 30 as police say negligence is ‘primary theory’
item.description: Bar owner in Thailand offers ‘deepest apologies for this tragic incident’ as police investigate whether exits were either blocked or hard to accessThe Bangkok pub that has become the scene of the city’s deadliest blaze in 17 years has said it will cooperate with an investigation into alleged negligence, as the death toll rose to 30. Death toll reaches 30 as police investigate negligence as ‘primary theory’.

item.title: World Cup football’s other goal: Helping young people talk about mental health
item.description: When Dr. Sahira Al Nahari founded Shifā Art, a Saudi Arabia-based organization using art to create conversations around mental health, she noticed that men attending her therapeutic art workshops often felt uncomfortable opening up about their feelings. World Cup football’s other goal: Helping young people talk about mental health.

item.title: ‘Cycle of escalation must end’: UN condemns deadly Strait of Hormuz attacks
item.description: The UN maritime agency, IMO, condemned overnight attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz that killed at least two seafarers as fresh strikes were reported early Tuesday in the escalating US-Iran war. ‘Cycle of escalation must end’: UN condemns deadly Strait of Hormuz attacks.

item.title: DRC Ebola outbreak is fastest-growing ever, warns WHO
item.description: Infections of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have reached record highs and a majority of new cases are coming from “unknown chains of transmission”, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Tuesday. DRC Ebola outbreak is fastest-growing ever, warns WHO.

item.title: US-Israel military merger bill a threat to American democracy
item.description: It’s called Section 219. Tucked away in the massive congressional spending bill known as the National Defense Authorization Act, or NDAA, this provision of the law would effectively require our nation to permanently entangle the American military with the Israeli military. Among other things, the United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative would require the US to share intellige US-Israel military merger bill a threat to American democracy.

item.title: China’s Africa lending model has a split personality
item.description: Over the past two decades, China’s rise as the world’s largest bilateral creditor has profoundly altered the global development finance landscape. Yet international scholarship on Chinese sovereign lending. especially to Africa. remains trapped in a binary: Western-centric “debt-trap diplomacy” narratives versus Beijing’s “South-South cooperative altruism” rhetoric. Understanding this requires m China’s Africa lending model has a split personality.

item.title: Indonesia-Singapore reset marks new era of ASEAN transactionalism
item.description: JAKARTA – The annual Indonesia-Singapore Leaders’ Retreat, held at Merdeka Palace in Jakarta on July 6, was more than a routine diplomatic exercise. With Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong presiding, the summit marked the full consolidation of a new generation of leadership in both nations. item.title: Ukraine’s robot army advancing on the war’s front lines
item.description: The Ukrainian military is steadily replacing dangerous frontline tasks with ground robots. In April, President Volodymyr Zelensky ordered the military to field at least 50,000 unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) in 2026, calling them “the next big step” in saving soldiers’ lives. item.title: Trump Walks Back Threat Of Hormuz Transit Fee; US Strikes Iran As Tehran Targets Gulf Shipping
item.description: US President Donald Trump has walked back his plan to charge a 20 percent fee on cargo shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, replacing it with proposed trade and investment agreements with Persian Gulf states while maintaining a blockade on Iranian shipping. Trump Walks Back Threat Of Hormuz Transit Fee; US Strikes Iran As Tehran Targets Gulf Shipping.

item.title: Zelenskyy Fights Another Political Battle With Another Cabinet Shake-Up In Ukraine
item.description: Zelenskyy gave no explanation for the unexpected shuffle of his Cabinet. But the popularity of Ukraine’s one-and-only wartime president is slipping, as war-weary voters tire of political scandals, as well as the unrelenting Russian invasion. Zelenskyy Fights Another Political Battle With Another Cabinet Shake-Up In Ukraine.

item.title: Aid deliveries to Gaza restricted, UN prepares El Nino response, El Salvador eliminates disease
item.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is calling for greater humanitarian access to Gaza, warning that restrictions on aid deliveries, ongoing violence and funding shortages are severely limiting its ability to reach people in need. Aid deliveries to Gaza restricted, UN prepares El Nino response, El Salvador eliminates disease.
